title: IMS registration and voice call · VoNR / VoLTE
description: Investigate why the Vanguard does not receive the MT call over VoNR and why the voice of the MO VoLTE call is unintelligible. Compare each symptom with the Solstice CDUT and decide whether there is one cause or two.

report.title: Issue Report — Challenge 4 · Voice over IMS

cen1-dut.title: IMS registration rejected: the MT call never arrives
cen1-dut.description: Vanguard · airplane mode toggle + MT call over VoNR · n78 PCI 88 · three repetitions

evidence.title: Authorization with the wrong nonce
evidence.html: The 401 carries nonce="N1-7f3a9c1e4b", but REGISTER CSeq 2 answers with nonce="N0-000000-init", a cached value that survived the airplane mode toggle.

evidence.title: Always one challenge behind
evidence.html: The cache is only updated after the 403. In REGISTER CSeq 4 the DUT uses N1-7f3a9c1e4b, while the latest challenge was already N2-8d5e0f2a91.

evidence.title: No IMS, no voice in 5G SA
evidence.html: After 2 rejections the IMS client abandons registration and Voice Domain Selection concludes ims_voice_over_nr: not available. The log ends with no paging and no INVITE.

evidence.title: Radio, NAS and PDU are fine
evidence.html: 5G SA Registration Accept and both PDU sessions (internet and IMS) are accepted before the first REGISTER, just as on the CDUT.

cen1-dut.notice: Log of repetition 01. Repetitions 02 and 03 (403 at 0.104/0.212 s and 0.116/0.231 s) come from the case document. The test bench uses SIP Digest MD5 instead of IMS-AKA. The UE log does not show the P-CSCF/S-CSCF side; the reason for the 403 comes from the response's Warning header.
cen1-dut.logLabel: Source: Desafio_S04_Log_Cen1_MT_VoNR_DUT_Vanguard.html · scenario 1, repetition 01 · 66 events · 5.9 s. Original log, unchanged.

guide.title: Airplane mode toggle
guide.text: The procedure restarts the IMS client without rebooting the device: 5G deregistration and radio off for about 1.4 s. Keep this in mind: what survives a toggle does not survive a power cycle.

guide.title: 5G SA registers normally
guide.text: Authentication, Security Mode and Registration Accept follow the same sequence and timing as the CDUT. Radio and NAS do not diverge.

guide.title: IMS PDU session ready
guide.text: PDU session 2 (IMS) accepted. SIP registration with the P-CSCF starts here.

guide.title: REGISTER #1: T 0
guide.text: First REGISTER, with an empty Authorization (CSeq 1), as the Digest flow requires. The case times are counted from here.

guide.title: 401: challenge N1
guide.text: WWW-Authenticate: Digest nonce="N1-7f3a9c1e4b", qop=auth, MD5. To answer, the UE must use exactly this nonce.

guide.title: Authorization built with a CACHED nonce
guide.text: The internal event shows the error: "using CACHED nonce N0-000000-init". At the same point the CDUT uses the challenge nonce ("using challenge nonce").

guide.title: 1st 403 Forbidden at T +0.110 s
guide.text: Warning: 399 "nonce does not match latest challenge". The network says exactly what is wrong: the nonce, not the password or the identity.

guide.title: Cache updated too late
guide.text: Only now does the cache move to N1. The DUT restarts with REGISTER #3 without Authorization and gets a fresh challenge, N2-8d5e0f2a91.

guide.title: One challenge behind again
guide.text: "using CACHED nonce N1-7f3a9c1e4b": the DUT answers the previous challenge, not the current one (N2). If the "init" value alone were the defect, this attempt would have passed.

guide.title: 2nd 403 Forbidden at T +0.220 s
guide.text: Same Warning 399. This is the second rejected authenticated attempt.

guide.title: IMS registration abandoned
guide.text: max_auth_attempts = 2 reached: ims_state DEREGISTERED. The client does not try again.

guide.title: No voice in 5G SA
guide.text: Voice Domain Selection: IMS not registered, no CS domain reachable from 5GS, and the UE stays in 5G SA without voice. The remote terminal's call cannot be delivered: the log ends with no paging and no INVITE.

cen1-cdut.title: Registered on the 1st attempt, MT call answered
cen1-cdut.description: Solstice · same airplane mode toggle + MT call over VoNR · n78 PCI 88 · three repetitions

evidence.title: Answers the current challenge
evidence.html: After the 401 with nonce="N1-5c20e9b7d1", REGISTER CSeq 2 uses the same nonce and the 200 OK arrives at T +0.102 s.

evidence.title: Same procedure as the DUT
evidence.html: Same cell (PCI 88), same SIP realm, same airplane mode toggle and the same remote terminal originating the call.

evidence.title: MT call delivered
evidence.html: Paging → RRC Setup mt-Access → INVITE → 183 → QoS preconditions (5QI 1) → 180 Ringing → 200 OK. EVS vocoder on PT 97, the same as in the SDP.

evidence.title: Contrast localizes, it does not prove
evidence.html: The CDUT shows that the network and realm accept Digest MD5 on the 1st attempt. The DUT's internal mechanism comes from the Authorization Build events in the Vanguard's own log.

cen1-cdut.notice: Log of repetition 01. The 200 OK times of repetitions 02 and 03 (0.098 s and 0.109 s) come from the case document. The MT call arrives about 12 s after registration, when the remote terminal places the call; the replay compresses long gaps.
cen1-cdut.logLabel: Source: Desafio_S04_Log_Cen1_MT_VoNR_CDUT_Solstice.html · scenario 1, repetition 01 · 97 events · 34.1 s. Original log, unchanged.

guide.title: REGISTER #1: T 0
guide.text: Same sequence as the DUT so far: airplane mode toggle, 5G SA registration and two PDU sessions.

guide.title: 401 with nonce N1
guide.text: nonce="N1-5c20e9b7d1", qop=auth, MD5, realm ims.novalink.com.br.

guide.title: Authorization with the challenge nonce
guide.text: "using challenge nonce N1-5c20e9b7d1". This is the exact point where the DUT diverges: there it reads "using CACHED nonce".

guide.title: 200 OK at T +0.102 s
guide.text: IMS registration completed on the 1st authenticated attempt, followed by the reg-event SUBSCRIBE/NOTIFY.

guide.title: Paging: the network reaches the UE
guide.text: With IMS registered, the remote terminal's call becomes paging in 5G SA. The UE answers with RRC Setup, establishmentCause mt-Access.

guide.title: MT INVITE with SDP offer
guide.text: The network offers EVS (PT 97), AMR-WB (96/99), AMR (98/101) and DTMF. Here the network is the offerer and PT 97 is EVS on both sides.

guide.title: Voice bearer: 5QI 1
guide.text: PDU session modification with QFI 2 / 5QI 1 (GBR 53 kbps). The QoS preconditions are met on both ends in the UPDATE.

guide.title: 180 Ringing
guide.text: The device rings: the MT call was delivered, the opposite of the DUT.

guide.title: EVS vocoder on PT 97
guide.text: EVS 24.4 kbps SWB on PT 97: the vocoder codec is the one the SDP binds to PT 97.

guide.title: RTP at T+10 s
guide.text: TX 500 / RX 498 packets on PT 97, with clear audio.

cen2-dut.title: Call established, unintelligible voice
cen2-dut.description: Vanguard · power cycle + MO call over VoLTE · Band 3 EARFCN 1575 PCI 41 · three repetitions

timelineLabels.note: Seconds since INVITE · marks: INVITE, 183, 200 OK; vocoder start, RTP at T+10 s, BYE

metrics.label: IMS registration
metrics.note: 200 OK in 0.110 s · after power cycle

evidence.title: Same number, different codecs
evidence.html: The DUT's INVITE declares a=rtpmap:97 EVS/16000 (AMR/8000 is PT 98). The network's answer in the 183 picks AMR and labels it a=rtpmap:97 AMR/8000.

evidence.title: The DUT ignores the answer's rtpmap
evidence.html: In the UPDATE the DUT re-offers PT 97 = EVS/16000, and the network again answers PT 97 = AMR/8000. The vocoder starts as EVS 24.4 kbps (SWB), PT 97.

evidence.title: Transport and QoS are normal
evidence.html: QCI 1 dedicated bearer (GBR 53 kbps), preconditions met and TX 500 / RX 498 at T+10 s: the packets arrive, but are decoded with the wrong codec.

evidence.title: No IMS registration defect here
evidence.html: After the power cycle the nonce cache is empty (cache empty → using challenge nonce) and registration passes on the 1st attempt. The scenario 1 symptom does not appear.

cen2-dut.notice: Log of repetition 01. The RTP counters of repetitions 02 and 03 (RX 497 and 499) come from the case document. This is a UE log: it does not show the payload the network actually sends, only the SDPs exchanged and the vocoder the DUT selected.
cen2-dut.logLabel: Source: Desafio_S04_Log_Cen2_MO_VoLTE_DUT_Vanguard.html · scenario 2, repetition 01 · 101 events · 25.7 s. Original log, unchanged.

guide.title: Full power cycle
guide.text: Unlike scenario 1, the device is fully rebooted here. Keep this contrast in mind when ruling out hypotheses.

guide.title: Empty nonce cache
guide.text: "cache empty -> using challenge nonce": with no stale value cached, the DUT answers the right challenge.

guide.title: IMS registered on the 1st attempt
guide.text: 200 OK in 0.110 s, practically the same as the CDUT (0.101 s). The scenario 1 authentication defect does not show up: same SIM, same credentials.

guide.title: MO INVITE: the DUT's offer
guide.text: m=audio 42010 RTP/AVP 97 96 99 98 101 102 103. The DUT numbers: 97 = EVS/16000, 96/99 = AMR-WB, 98/101 = AMR/8000. This is T 0.

guide.title: 183: the network picks AMR and calls it 97
guide.text: SDP answer m=audio 36020 RTP/AVP 97 103 with a=rtpmap:97 AMR/8000. The network selected AMR (narrowband) but reused number 97, which for the DUT is EVS. This is the exact point of divergence.

guide.title: DUT UPDATE: 97 is still EVS
guide.text: The DUT re-offers m=audio 42010 RTP/AVP 97 103 with a=rtpmap:97 EVS/16000. It did not adopt the answer's codec. Compare with the CDUT, whose UPDATE already re-offers 97 = AMR/8000.

guide.title: UPDATE 200 OK: the network insists
guide.text: Again a=rtpmap:97 AMR/8000. Within one session, PT 97 now has two meanings: EVS for the DUT, AMR for the network.

guide.title: Call answered, no SIP error
guide.text: All signalling was accepted: no 4xx/5xx, QCI 1 bearer active. Nothing in the call flow flags a failure, which makes the defect hard to see without reading the SDP.

guide.title: EVS vocoder on PT 97
guide.text: "EVS 24.4 kbps (SWB), PT 97". On the CDUT the same event shows "AMR-NB 12.2 kbps, PT 97". The DUT encodes and decodes EVS while the far end uses AMR.

guide.title: Normal RTP, garbled audio
guide.text: TX 500 / RX 498 on PT 97, practically the same as the CDUT (RX 497). There is no packet loss: the problem is the codec, not the transport.

guide.title: BYE: unintelligible voice
guide.text: The user ends the call ("audio unintelligible"). The symptom repeats in 3 of 3 repetitions.

cen2-cdut.title: Same signalling, clear audio
cen2-cdut.description: Solstice · power cycle + MO call over VoLTE · Band 3 EARFCN 1575 PCI 41 · three repetitions

timelineLabels.note: Seconds since INVITE · marks: INVITE, 183, 200 OK; vocoder start, RTP at T+10 s, BYE

metrics.label: Network SDP · PT 97
metrics.note: same as offered by the CDUT

evidence.title: Consistent payload type map
evidence.html: The CDUT offers 97 = AMR/8000 (EVS is 107), and the network answers a=rtpmap:97 AMR/8000: the same number with the same codec on both sides.

evidence.title: UPDATE follows the answer
evidence.html: The UPDATE re-offers only 97 = AMR/8000, the negotiated codec, and the vocoder starts as AMR-NB 12.2 kbps, PT 97.

evidence.title: Same signalling and counters
evidence.html: Same 183, PRACK, QCI 1 bearer, UPDATE, 180 and 200 OK timing as the DUT. RTP at TX 500 / RX 497, practically the same as the DUT.

evidence.title: The control does not exercise remapping
evidence.html: The CDUT's numbering matches the network's, so this log does not show how the Solstice would handle a payload type renumbered in the answer. The contrast localizes the defect in the DUT; the mechanism comes from the Vanguard's own SDPs.

guide.title: IMS registered on the 1st attempt
guide.text: Same flow as the DUT after the power cycle: empty cache, challenge nonce, 200 OK in 0.101 s.

guide.title: MO INVITE: the CDUT's offer
guide.text: m=audio 40020 RTP/AVP 107 104 110 97 108 105 100. The CDUT numbers: 107 = EVS, 104/110 = AMR-WB, 97/108 = AMR/8000. This is T 0.

guide.title: 183: the network picks AMR on 97
guide.text: a=rtpmap:97 AMR/8000, the same number and codec the CDUT offered. No ambiguity.

guide.title: UPDATE with the negotiated codec
guide.text: The CDUT re-offers m=audio 40020 RTP/AVP 97 100 with a=rtpmap:97 AMR/8000. The offer follows the previous answer.

guide.title: AMR-NB vocoder on PT 97
guide.text: "AMR-NB 12.2 kbps, PT 97": the vocoder uses the codec the SDP binds to PT 97. On the DUT this same event shows EVS.

guide.title: RTP at T+10 s
guide.text: TX 500 / RX 497 on PT 97, practically the same counters as the DUT, with clear audio. The difference is the codec, not the packets.
